vulnerability: Public arbitrary token burn / unauthorized token destruction
reason: The burn function is public and calls _transferFrom(account, DEAD, _amount) without checking that msg.sender is authorized to spend account's tokens or that the caller owns the tokens. The external transferFrom function checks allowances, but burn bypasses that check entirely. An attacker can call burn(victim, amount) to burn any holder's tokens, including the owner (who is tx-limit exempt, allowing the entire balance to be burned in one transaction) or the token contract's accumulated fee tokens. This can destroy user funds, prevent fee swapping/liquidity provision, manipulate AMM reserves by burning from the pair (with repeated calls up to the tx limit), and potentially facilitate price manipulation after calling pair.sync(). The impact is critical.

vulnerability: Sandwich attack due to zero slippage (amountOutMin=0)
reason: swapBack calls router.swapExactTokensForETHSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens with amountOutMin=0 and also calls router.addLiquidityETH with amountTokenMin=0 and amountETHMin=0. Because swapBack is triggered automatically inside user transfers when the token contract's fee balance exceeds swapThreshold, an attacker can watch the mempool for a transaction that will trigger swapBack, front-run the pool with a large swap to manipulate the token/WBNB price, let the victim's transaction execute the fee swap at the manipulated rate, then back-run to restore the price and profit. The contract accepts any output amount, so the attacker can extract most of the value of the fee tokens meant for liquidity, reflection, and marketing. This is a real-world MEV sandwich attack.

vulnerability: Fee denominator can be set to zero causing division-by-zero DoS
reason: setFees allows an authorized account (by default the owner) to set _feeDenominator to 0 as long as all fee values are also 0. The require checks use feeDenominator / 10 and feeDenominator / 5; when feeDenominator is 0 and fees are 0, both checks pass. After this state change, takeFee computes amount.mul(getTotalFee(...)).div(feeDenominator). On any taxable buy or sell, getTotalFee returns totalBuyFee or totalSellFee (0), so the code performs amount.mul(0).div(0), which reverts due to division by zero. Consequently, all buys and sells revert, trapping holders' funds and preventing trading. A malicious or compromised owner/authorized account can use this to brick the token's market and extort or harm holders.
